config.title: Card Component

intro.title: Card Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Card component that displays structured information, like a title, description, and image, in a clean layout. You will learn how to create a React functional component using JSX to define its structure and style it with CSS. The core programming concept is component composition, where you combine multiple elements into a single, reusable unit. You will use props to pass data into the component, making it dynamic and flexible for different content. This exercise introduces key React fundamentals while creating a practical UI element common in web applications.
intro.usecase: Card components are a foundational UI pattern used across modern web applications to present grouped information in a clean, contained layout. You'll see them in e-commerce product listings, social media feeds displaying posts, and dashboard widgets showing metrics or alerts. As a developer, you'll frequently build and customize cards to display user profiles, articles, or any modular content block that requires a consistent visual structure with optional actions like buttons or links.

objectives: Construct a functional React component that returns a card structure
Initialize and manage state variables for card content and visibility
Implement event handlers to control card interactions
Apply props to customize card appearance and content
Render dynamic content within card elements using JavaScript expressions
Bind user interface events to component handler functions
Configure conditional rendering based on component state

steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: Import React from the 'react' package at the top of the file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file so you can use JSX and create components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use in your component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React from the 'react' package. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React from 'react' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create Card component function
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Card that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called Card that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React from 'react';

// Create the Card component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component function is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The Card component is defined as a function and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the component, but make sure it's named exactly 'Card' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Card that returns null.

steps.title: Add component props parameter
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to the Card function to receive data.
steps.hint: In the function signature, add parentheses with a parameter named 'props'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card function should have a props parameter in its signature.
successCriteria: The Card function includes a props parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Card function has a parameter named 'props'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card function still doesn't have a props parameter. Add 'props' inside the parentheses of the function.

steps.title: Destructure props for title and content
steps.instruction: Inside the Card function, destructure the props parameter to extract title and content properties.
steps.hint: Use curly braces inside the function parameter to destructure title and content directly from props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card function should have destructured parameters: title and content.
successCriteria: The Card function signature includes destructured title and content parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're destructuring both title and content directly in the function parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try using curly braces inside the function parameter to extract title and content from props.

steps.title: Add main div container with card class
steps.instruction: Inside the Card component's return statement, replace `null` with a `<div>` element that has `className='card'`.
steps.hint: Return a JSX div element with the className attribute set to 'card'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component now returns a div element with the class 'card' as its main container.
successCriteria: The Card component returns a div element with className='card'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with className='card'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component should return a div with className='card'.

steps.title: Add heading element for card title
steps.instruction: Inside the card div, add an h2 element that displays the title prop.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax to create an h2 element and insert the title prop inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The card component will have a heading that shows the title passed as a prop.
successCriteria: An h2 element is added inside the div, and it displays the title prop using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an h2 element, but make sure it displays the title prop using curly braces like {title}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h2 element is missing or doesn't display the title prop correctly. Check the JSX syntax.

steps.title: Add paragraph element for card content
steps.instruction: Inside the Card component, add a paragraph element below the heading to display the content prop.
steps.hint:
Use a

element with the content variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: paragraph element with dynamic content

{description}
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component will now display both a title heading and a content paragraph.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added below the h2, displaying the content prop value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the content prop value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or not correctly displaying the content prop.

steps.title: Export Card component
steps.instruction: Export the Card component as the default export so it can be imported in other files.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Exporting a function as default
export default function greet() {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component is exported as the default export, making it available for import elsewhere.
successCriteria: Card component is exported as default
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't exported correctly. Use 'export default' syntax.

steps.title: Create App component and import Card
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named App that imports and uses the Card component with sample title and content props.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX containing the Card component with hardcoded props like title='Sample Title' and content='Sample content text'.
steps.expectedOutcome: An App component is created that renders the Card component with sample data passed as props.
successCriteria: The App component is defined as a function, imports the Card component, and returns JSX containing <Card title="..." content="..." /> with sample values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your App component returns JSX containing the Card component with both title and content props provided.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined or doesn't use the Card component with props. Try creating a function named App that returns <Card title="Sample" content="Text" />.

steps.title: Render multiple Card instances with different data
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render at least two Card components with different title and content props.
steps.hint: Add multiple <Card /> elements inside the return statement, each with different values for the title and content props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display multiple Card components with different titles and content when rendered.
successCriteria: The App component renders at least two Card components with distinct title and content props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have at least two Card components with different title and content props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't yet render multiple Card components with different props. Try adding at least two <Card /> elements with distinct title and content values.
